t: This is a statue of Samuel Bourne Bevington, standing on Tooley Street in Bermondsey. It is Grade II listed. Bevington was a businessman, philanthropist and local politician, and he became the first mayor of the newly established Metropolitan Borough of Bermondsey, where he was widely popular. That popularity is why he is honoured here, in the borough he served. The sculptor was Sydney March, an English artist best known for portrait busts of royalty and contemporary figures, and for war memorials. He and his siblings also completed the National War Memorial of Canada in Ottawa.
